repairs.title: The Ozone Layer Is Recovering
repairs.summary: Global action phased down ozone-depleting chemicals, and the ozone layer is on a path toward recovery.
repairs.why_it_matters: It proves international environmental agreements can work when the problem is clear and enforcement is real.
repairs.caveat: Recovery is still ongoing and depends on continued compliance.

repairs.title: Smallpox Was Eradicated
repairs.summary: In 1980, the WHO declared smallpox eradicated after a global vaccination and surveillance campaign.
repairs.why_it_matters: A disease that killed millions was removed from everyday human life by organized public health work.
repairs.caveat: Smallpox is exceptional; most diseases cannot be eradicated this cleanly.

repairs.title: More Children Survive
repairs.summary: The global under-five mortality rate declined by about 60 percent between 1990 and 2024.
repairs.why_it_matters: This is quiet progress measured in millions of families spared grief.
repairs.caveat: The remaining burden is still unacceptable and progress is uneven.

repairs.title: Clean Water Reached More Homes
repairs.summary: Between 2015 and 2024, 961 million people gained access to safely managed drinking water services.
repairs.why_it_matters: Better water access prevents disease and gives people time back from collecting water.
repairs.caveat: Billions still lack safely managed drinking water.

repairs.title: Extreme Poverty Fell
repairs.summary: The number of people living in extreme poverty fell from about 2.31 billion in 1990 to about 808 million in 2025.
repairs.why_it_matters: Large-scale material progress is possible, even if it is fragile and uneven.
repairs.caveat: Recent shocks and inequality mean this progress is not guaranteed to continue.

repairs.title: Literacy Became Normal
repairs.summary: Two centuries ago, only a small minority of people could read and write; today more than four out of five people can.
repairs.why_it_matters: Education changes what ordinary people can understand, build, question, and pass on.
repairs.caveat: School access and learning quality still vary sharply by region and income.

repairs.title: AIDS Deaths Fell
repairs.summary: AIDS-related deaths have fallen sharply since their peak in 2004 and are much lower than in 2010.
repairs.why_it_matters: Treatment access and sustained public health programs can turn a terrifying epidemic into a more survivable condition for many.
repairs.caveat: Funding gaps and unequal access still put lives at risk.

repairs.title: Birth Became Safer
repairs.summary: From 2000 to 2023, the global maternal mortality ratio declined by about 40 percent.
repairs.why_it_matters: Skilled care, emergency treatment, and stronger health systems save mothers' lives.
repairs.caveat: Too many preventable deaths still occur, especially where care is underfunded or disrupted.

repairs.title: Clean Power Keeps Growing
repairs.summary: Renewables supplied about 32 percent of global electricity in 2024, with the share projected to rise through 2030.
repairs.why_it_matters: The energy system is not fixed in place; infrastructure can shift when technology, policy, and cost line up.
repairs.caveat: Electricity is only part of total energy use, and grid buildout remains a serious bottleneck.

repairs.title: Leaded Petrol Ended
repairs.summary: In 2021, the last country using leaded petrol phased it out, ending legal road use worldwide.
repairs.why_it_matters: A toxic product that harmed children's brains was removed through a long, coordinated campaign.
repairs.caveat: Legacy lead pollution remains in soil, dust, and older infrastructure.

repairs.title: Air Pollution Death Rates Fell
repairs.summary: Global death rates from total air pollution have nearly halved since 1990, mainly because indoor air pollution declined.
repairs.why_it_matters: Cleaner fuels, better technology, and public health work can make invisible risks less deadly.
repairs.caveat: Outdoor air pollution remains a major global health problem.

repairs.title: Mountain Gorillas Increased
repairs.summary: Conservation work helped mountain gorilla populations recover to more than 1,000 individuals in the wild.
repairs.why_it_matters: Species decline is not always one-way when protection is persistent and local conservation works.
repairs.caveat: Mountain gorillas remain endangered and depend on continued protection.

repairs.title: Polio Was Pushed Back
repairs.summary: Wild poliovirus cases have decreased by more than 99 percent since 1988.
repairs.why_it_matters: Vaccination campaigns turned a once-common cause of paralysis into a disease now cornered in only a few places.
repairs.caveat: Polio is not eradicated yet, and outbreaks can return where immunization is weak.

repairs.title: Guinea Worm Nearly Vanished
repairs.summary: Guinea worm disease fell from about 3.5 million human cases a year in 1986 to 10 cases in 2025.
repairs.why_it_matters: A painful parasitic disease was beaten back mostly through clean water, education, and local surveillance.
repairs.caveat: The last cases are hard, especially because infections in animals can keep transmission alive.

repairs.title: Trachoma Lost Ground
repairs.summary: By July 2026, WHO had validated 32 countries as having eliminated trachoma as a public health problem.
repairs.why_it_matters: Millions of people are less exposed to a preventable infectious cause of blindness.
repairs.caveat: Elimination as a public health problem does not mean the infection has disappeared everywhere.

repairs.title: River Blindness Was Cleared
repairs.summary: WHO has verified five countries as free of onchocerciasis after decades of elimination work.
repairs.why_it_matters: Mass treatment and surveillance can remove a disease that causes severe skin disease and vision loss.
repairs.caveat: Many people, especially in parts of Africa, remain at risk.

repairs.title: Open Defecation Fell
repairs.summary: Between 2000 and 2022, the number of people practising open defecation fell from 1.3 billion to 419 million.
repairs.why_it_matters: Sanitation progress cuts disease risk and gives people more safety, privacy, and dignity.
repairs.caveat: Hundreds of millions of people still lack basic sanitation.

repairs.title: Child Labour Declined
repairs.summary: Since 2000, child labour has almost halved, falling from 246 million children to 138 million.
repairs.why_it_matters: Fewer children are losing childhood, school, and health to work they should not have to do.
repairs.caveat: The world missed its elimination target, and progress is still far too slow.

repairs.title: Acid Rain Was Reduced
repairs.summary: From 1995 to 2023, annual sulfur dioxide emissions from U.S. power plants fell by 95 percent.
repairs.why_it_matters: A major pollution problem was reduced through enforceable rules, monitoring, and cleaner technology.
repairs.caveat: This is a U.S. example, and power-sector progress does not fix all air pollution.

repairs.title: Bald Eagles Came Back
repairs.summary: The lower-48 bald eagle population rose from about 487 breeding pairs in 1963 to 9,789 pairs by 2007.
repairs.why_it_matters: Banning DDT, protecting habitat, and enforcing wildlife law helped reverse a visible collapse.
repairs.caveat: Recovery still depends on habitat protection and long-term monitoring.

repairs.title: Iberian Lynx Rebounded
repairs.summary: The Iberian lynx rose from 62 mature individuals in 2001 to 648 in 2022, with the total population now over 2,000.
repairs.why_it_matters: Focused breeding, reintroduction, and habitat work pulled the world's rarest cat away from the edge.
repairs.caveat: Road deaths, prey decline, and habitat fragmentation still threaten the recovery.

repairs.title: Pandas Became Less Endangered
repairs.summary: Giant pandas were downlisted from Endangered to Vulnerable after their population increased by 17 percent in a decade.
repairs.why_it_matters: Habitat protection and long conservation work changed the trajectory for a species people had nearly written off.
repairs.caveat: Vulnerable still means at risk, especially where habitats are fragmented.

repairs.title: More Nature Is Protected
repairs.summary: In 2024, protected and conserved areas covered 17.6 percent of land and inland waters and 8.4 percent of marine areas.
repairs.why_it_matters: More ecosystems now have at least some formal protection instead of being left entirely exposed.
repairs.caveat: Coverage is not the same as good management, and the world is still short of the 2030 target.

repairs.title: Road Deaths Fell Slightly
repairs.summary: WHO estimated annual road traffic deaths fell to 1.19 million, a 5 percent drop from 2010 to 2021.
repairs.why_it_matters: Design, rules, vehicles, and emergency care can make everyday mobility less deadly.
repairs.caveat: The toll is still enormous, and low- and middle-income countries carry most of it.

repairs.title: Measles Deaths Dropped
repairs.summary: Global measles deaths fell by 88 percent between 2000 and 2024, largely because vaccination reached more children.
repairs.why_it_matters: A familiar vaccine prevented millions of deaths from a disease that still spreads fast when protection slips.
repairs.caveat: Cases and outbreaks have risen again, so this repair depends on sustained immunization.

repairs.title: Fewer Adults Use Tobacco
repairs.summary: WHO estimates that about 1 in 5 adults used tobacco in 2022, down from about 1 in 3 in 2000.
repairs.why_it_matters: Taxes, warnings, smoke-free rules, and cessation support can shift a huge public-health risk.
repairs.caveat: Tobacco still kills millions each year, and industry pressure keeps the problem alive.

repairs.title: Electricity Reached More People
repairs.summary: Since 2010, about 800 million people have gained access to electricity.
repairs.why_it_matters: Light, refrigeration, communication, and safer work become possible when reliable power reaches a home.
repairs.caveat: Hundreds of millions still live without electricity, and progress has been uneven.

repairs.title: Cleaner Cooking Spread
repairs.summary: Since 2010, about 1.5 billion people have gained access to clean cooking.
repairs.why_it_matters: Cleaner cooking reduces household smoke, one of the everyday hazards that quietly damages health.
repairs.caveat: Many households still rely on polluting fuels, especially where energy access is fragile.

repairs.title: Safer Sanitation Expanded
repairs.summary: Between 2015 and 2024, 1.2 billion people gained access to safely managed sanitation services.
repairs.why_it_matters: Sanitation prevents disease while giving people more privacy, safety, and dignity.
repairs.caveat: Billions still lack safely managed sanitation, so the repair is large but unfinished.

repairs.title: Hepatitis B Fell In Children
repairs.summary: WHO estimates chronic hepatitis B infection in children under five fell from about 5 percent before vaccines to under 1 percent in 2019.
repairs.why_it_matters: Infant vaccination prevents lifelong infection and future liver disease.
repairs.caveat: Birth-dose coverage is still uneven, and many adults already living with hepatitis B need care.

repairs.title: Iodized Salt Protected Brains
repairs.summary: UNICEF reports that 89 percent of people worldwide consume iodized salt.
repairs.why_it_matters: A small nutrition fix helps prevent iodine deficiency, which can harm pregnancy and early brain development.
repairs.caveat: Coverage is not universal, and iodine status still needs monitoring.

repairs.title: Neglected Diseases Lost Ground
repairs.summary: The population requiring neglected tropical disease interventions fell from 2.19 billion in 2010 to 1.4 billion in 2024.
repairs.why_it_matters: Mass treatment, surveillance, and basic public-health delivery can shrink diseases that mostly affect poor communities.
repairs.caveat: More than a billion people still require treatment or care.

repairs.title: A Livestock Plague Ended
repairs.summary: Rinderpest was declared eradicated in 2011, the first animal disease eradicated worldwide.
repairs.why_it_matters: Veterinary science and coordinated surveillance removed a disease that devastated cattle, wildlife, and food security.
repairs.caveat: Eradication requires strict lab containment so the virus cannot escape back into the world.

repairs.title: More Girls Went To School
repairs.summary: UNESCO reports 49.1 million more girls in primary and secondary school in 2023 than in 2015.
repairs.why_it_matters: Education expands choices, safety, income, and political voice across a lifetime.
repairs.caveat: Completion and learning gaps remain, especially for girls facing poverty or conflict.

repairs.title: Solar Power Got Cheap
repairs.summary: IRENA reports that utility-scale solar PV electricity costs fell sharply between 2010 and 2023.
repairs.why_it_matters: Cheaper clean power makes energy transition less dependent on sacrifice and more dependent on deployment.
repairs.caveat: Cheap generation still needs grids, storage, permitting, and fair supply chains.

repairs.title: Fewer Children Miss School
repairs.summary: UNESCO estimates that out-of-school numbers fell by 33 percent between 2000 and 2015.
repairs.why_it_matters: School access improved for many children during a period of focused global education investment.
repairs.caveat: Progress has stalled and partly reversed since 2015.

repairs.title: Tanker Oil Spills Fell
repairs.summary: ITOPF reports that oil lost from tanker spills in the 2010s was 95 percent lower than in the 1970s.
repairs.why_it_matters: Rules, ship design, navigation, and response systems made a dirty global industry less accident-prone.
repairs.caveat: Oil spills still happen, and this metric covers tankers rather than all oil pollution.

repairs.title: Sea Turtles Rebounded
repairs.summary: NOAA reports that most tracked sea turtle nesting sites now show increases, including large gains for some loggerhead populations.
repairs.why_it_matters: Protecting nests, habitat, and fisheries interactions can let long-lived species recover.
repairs.caveat: All sea turtle species in U.S. waters remain protected, and climate change adds new pressure.

repairs.title: Children Carry Less Lead
repairs.summary: EPA reports U.S. children's median blood lead level fell 96 percent from 1976-1980 to 2017-2020.
repairs.why_it_matters: Removing lead from fuel, paint, and products measurably reduced a toxin that harms developing brains.
repairs.caveat: No level of lead exposure is safe, and older housing and pipes still create unequal risks.

repairs.title: Mercury Products Were Curbed
repairs.summary: The Minamata Convention set controls to phase out or reduce mercury in many products and processes.
repairs.why_it_matters: A known neurotoxin is being pushed out of everyday commerce through a global treaty.
repairs.caveat: Mercury pollution persists, and treaty implementation varies by country and sector.

repairs.title: More Adults Got Accounts
repairs.summary: World Bank data shows global account ownership rose from 51 percent of adults in 2011 to 79 percent in 2024.
repairs.why_it_matters: Basic accounts can make saving, receiving pay, sending money, and handling shocks easier.
repairs.caveat: An account does not guarantee financial security, and many people remain excluded.

repairs.title: More Children Were Counted
repairs.summary: UNICEF says birth registration for children under five rose from about 60 percent in 2000 to 77 percent today.
repairs.why_it_matters: A birth record helps children claim identity, services, school access, and legal protection.
repairs.caveat: About 150 million children under five still remain unregistered.

repairs.title: More Births Had Skilled Care
repairs.summary: WHO data shows births attended by skilled health personnel rose from 61 percent in 2000 to 87 percent in 2025.
repairs.why_it_matters: Trained care during childbirth is one of the practical ways health systems keep mothers and newborns alive.
repairs.caveat: Attendance does not prove care quality, and access remains uneven.

repairs.title: Landmine Stockpiles Shrank
repairs.summary: Landmine Monitor reports that 94 Mine Ban Treaty states have destroyed more than 55 million stockpiled antipersonnel mines.
repairs.why_it_matters: Destroying stockpiles removes weapons designed to keep harming civilians long after fighting ends.
repairs.caveat: Landmines are still being used, and casualties have recently risen in some conflicts.

repairs.title: Drowning Death Rates Fell
repairs.summary: WHO reports that the global drowning death rate dropped by 38 percent between 2000 and 2021.
repairs.why_it_matters: Prevention, safer environments, and better public-health attention can reduce a quiet cause of sudden loss.
repairs.caveat: More than 300,000 people still died from drowning in 2021, and progress is uneven.

repairs.title: Clean Energy Work Grew
repairs.summary: IRENA reports that global renewable energy jobs rose to 16.2 million in 2023, up from 13.7 million in 2022.
repairs.why_it_matters: The energy transition is not only machinery; it is also a growing base of people trained to build and maintain it.
repairs.caveat: Jobs are unevenly distributed by region, technology, and working conditions.

repairs.title: One Treaty Also Cooled The Future
repairs.summary: UNEP's Ozone Secretariat says cuts in ozone-depleting substances are estimated to avoid about 0.5 to 1 degrees Celsius of warming by mid-century.
repairs.why_it_matters: A treaty built for one environmental crisis also reduced a major climate risk.
repairs.caveat: The avoided-warming estimate depends on comparison scenarios and continued compliance.

repairs.title: More People Came Online
repairs.summary: ITU estimated that 5.5 billion people were online in 2024, about 68 percent of the world's population.
repairs.why_it_matters: Connectivity can widen access to information, services, work, and community when it is affordable and usable.
repairs.caveat: A third of humanity remained offline in 2024, and access quality is deeply unequal.

repairs.title: Fewer Girls Became Child Brides
repairs.summary: UNICEF reports that the share of young women married as children fell from about one in four a decade ago to about one in five.
repairs.why_it_matters: Delayed marriage can protect girls' schooling, health, autonomy, and childhood.
repairs.caveat: Progress is too slow for the 2030 goal, and conflict can quickly reverse gains.

repairs.title: Handwashing Reached More Homes
repairs.summary: UNICEF reported that access to basic hand hygiene at home rose from 5.0 billion people in 2015 to 5.5 billion in 2020.
repairs.why_it_matters: Soap and water at home are simple infrastructure that can prevent infection and protect daily life.
repairs.caveat: If trends continue, many people will still lack basic hand hygiene at the end of the decade.

repairs.title: Malaria Work Saved Millions
repairs.summary: WHO estimates that global malaria efforts averted 2.3 billion cases and 14 million deaths since 2000.
repairs.why_it_matters: Bed nets, testing, treatment, surveillance, and vaccines show that old diseases can still be pushed back.
repairs.caveat: Malaria deaths rose in some recent periods, and funding gaps threaten further progress.

repairs.title: TB Treatment Saved Lives
repairs.summary: WHO says global efforts to combat tuberculosis have saved an estimated 83 million lives since 2000.
repairs.why_it_matters: Diagnosis, treatment, and prevention can turn a deadly infection into something curable for many more people.
repairs.caveat: TB remains widespread, and drug-resistant TB is still a serious threat.

repairs.title: Newborn Tetanus Fell
repairs.summary: WHO estimates neonatal tetanus deaths fell by 88 percent from about 200,000 in 2000 to 24,000 in 2021.
repairs.why_it_matters: Vaccination, clean delivery, and umbilical-cord care can prevent a disease that kills newborns in their first days.
repairs.caveat: Several countries have not yet reached elimination status, and setbacks remain possible.

repairs.title: Fistula Surgeries Restored Lives
repairs.summary: UNFPA says its global campaign has supported more than 153,000 obstetric fistula repair surgeries.
repairs.why_it_matters: Repair surgery can restore health and dignity after a childbirth injury that often isolates women.
repairs.caveat: Many women still lack access to prevention, safe childbirth care, or surgery.

repairs.title: Vaccines Saved Generations
repairs.summary: WHO estimates that global immunization efforts have saved at least 154 million lives since 1974.
repairs.why_it_matters: Routine vaccination is ordinary infrastructure that quietly prevents death at enormous scale.
repairs.caveat: Coverage gaps, misinformation, and disrupted health systems can still reverse gains.

repairs.title: Fewer Children Got HIV
repairs.summary: UNICEF reports that new HIV infections among children aged 0 to 14 fell by about 69 percent since 2010.
repairs.why_it_matters: Preventing transmission during pregnancy, birth, and breastfeeding protects children before illness begins.
repairs.caveat: Children still miss testing and treatment, especially where health systems are strained.

repairs.title: Declared Chemical Weapons Were Destroyed
repairs.summary: In 2023, OPCW verified that all declared chemical weapons stockpiles had been irreversibly destroyed.
repairs.why_it_matters: Treaties, inspections, and patient destruction work removed a class of weapons built for mass suffering.
repairs.caveat: Undeclared weapons, alleged use, and toxic industrial chemicals remain serious risks.
repairs.source_name: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons

repairs.title: More Countries Ended Executions
repairs.summary: Amnesty reports that countries fully abolishing the death penalty rose from 16 in 1977 to 113 today.
repairs.why_it_matters: Legal systems can move away from irreversible state killing and toward stronger human-rights norms.
repairs.caveat: Executions still continue, and recent totals have risen sharply in some countries.

repairs.title: Nuclear Arsenals Shrunk
repairs.summary: FAS estimates global nuclear weapons fell from about 70,300 in 1986 to about 12,321 at the start of 2026.
repairs.why_it_matters: Arms control and post-Cold-War reductions show that even existential risks can be reduced.
repairs.caveat: Modernization, treaty breakdown, and new arms races keep nuclear danger very real.

repairs.title: Disaster Warnings Saved Lives
repairs.summary: WMO reports that deaths from weather, climate, and water hazards fell almost threefold from 1970 to 2019.
repairs.why_it_matters: Forecasts, warnings, evacuation systems, and disaster management turn knowledge into survival.
repairs.caveat: Economic losses rose, exposure is growing, and climate change can overwhelm weak systems.

repairs.title: Cancer Death Rates Fell
repairs.summary: The American Cancer Society reports that the U.S. cancer death rate fell by 34 percent from 1991 to 2022.
repairs.why_it_matters: Less smoking, earlier detection, and better treatment turned many diagnoses into longer lives.
repairs.caveat: This is U.S.-specific, and cancer incidence is rising for some groups and cancer types.

repairs.title: Home Fires Became Rarer
repairs.summary: NFPA reports that U.S. reported home fires fell from 3.2 per thousand people in 1980 to 1.1 in 2023.
repairs.why_it_matters: Building codes, alarms, safer products, and prevention work make everyday homes less deadly.
repairs.caveat: Fire deaths still happen, and risk remains much higher where prevention is weak.

repairs.title: More Women Entered Parliament
repairs.summary: UN Women reports that women hold 27.5 percent of parliamentary seats, up from 11 percent in 1995.
repairs.why_it_matters: Representation changes who is present when laws, budgets, and public priorities are decided.
repairs.caveat: Parity is still distant, and political power remains uneven within and beyond parliaments.

repairs.title: Cluster Munition Stockpiles Shrunk
repairs.summary: Cluster Munition Monitor says 42 States Parties destroyed all declared stocks, including 179 million submunitions.
repairs.why_it_matters: Destroying stockpiles prevents weapons that can harm civilians long after fighting ends from being used later.
repairs.caveat: Not all countries have joined the treaty, and cluster munitions are still used in conflicts.

repairs.title: Humpback Whales Recovered In Many Seas
repairs.summary: NOAA says nine of 14 humpback whale populations recovered enough that they no longer warrant listing.
repairs.why_it_matters: Limits on commercial whaling and long monitoring helped a depleted species rebound in many regions.
repairs.caveat: Several populations remain endangered or threatened, and warming oceans add new pressure.

repairs.title: More Students Finished School
repairs.summary: UNESCO reports global upper-secondary completion rose from 37 percent in 2000 to 61 percent in 2024.
repairs.why_it_matters: Finishing school gives young people more choices than enrolment alone and reflects years of sustained education investment.
repairs.caveat: Progress is slow and unequal, and 95 percent global completion remains many decades away at the current pace.

repairs.title: Saiga Antelopes Came Back
repairs.summary: Kazakhstan's saiga population recovered from about 39,000 in 2005 to nearly two million by 2023.
repairs.why_it_matters: Anti-poaching work, protected habitat, monitoring, and international cooperation rescued a species near collapse.
repairs.caveat: Disease, poaching, infrastructure, and conflict with agriculture can still reverse this unusually rapid recovery.

repairs.title: European Bison Returned
repairs.summary: IUCN moved European bison from Vulnerable to Near Threatened after the wild population grew from 1,800 in 2003 to over 6,200 in 2019.
repairs.why_it_matters: Breeding, reintroduction, and habitat management brought Europe's largest land mammal back after extinction in the wild.
repairs.caveat: Most herds remain isolated and small enough to face genetic, disease, and habitat risks.
repairs.source_name: International Union for Conservation of Nature

repairs.title: The Thames Came Back To Life
repairs.summary: The tidal Thames recovered after parts were declared biologically dead in 1957 and now supports fish, seals, and seahorses.
repairs.why_it_matters: Sewage treatment, pollution controls, and long monitoring show that even a heavily damaged urban river can recover.
repairs.caveat: Sewage spills, rising temperatures, and declining fish counts show that the recovery is incomplete.

repairs.title: Countries Cleaned Up The Rhine
repairs.summary: Rhine countries cut inputs of most priority pollutants from point sources by 70 to 100 percent between 1985 and 2000.
repairs.why_it_matters: Shared rules, wastewater treatment, and cross-border monitoring repaired a river running through many jurisdictions.
repairs.caveat: Agricultural nutrients, some pesticides, heavy metals, and barriers to migrating fish remain unresolved.
repairs.source_name: International Commission for the Protection of the Rhine

repairs.title: Forest Loss Slowed
repairs.summary: FAO reports annual deforestation slowed from 17.6 million hectares in 1990-2000 to 10.9 million in 2015-2025.
repairs.why_it_matters: Policy, protected areas, restoration, and changing land use have reduced the speed of a major global loss.
repairs.caveat: The world is still losing vast forest areas each year, especially in Africa and South America.

repairs.title: More Forests Got Long-Term Plans
repairs.summary: FAO reports 2.13 billion hectares of forest had management plans by 2025, 365 million more than in 1990.
repairs.why_it_matters: Documented, revisable plans turn forest protection from a promise into infrastructure for sustained management.
repairs.caveat: A plan does not guarantee good enforcement, and large forest areas still lack one.

repairs.title: Part Of The Aral Sea Returned
repairs.summary: A World Bank-backed dike raised water levels in the North Aral Sea and helped revive its fishing economy.
repairs.why_it_matters: Targeted engineering and water management restored a damaged ecosystem that many had written off entirely.
repairs.caveat: This recovery is limited to the northern basin; most of the wider Aral Sea disaster remains unresolved.

repairs.title: Battery Costs Collapsed
repairs.summary: IEA reports lithium-ion battery prices fell from about $1,400 per kilowatt-hour in 2010 to below $140 in 2023.
repairs.why_it_matters: Cheaper storage makes electric transport, renewable power, and off-grid electricity more practical.
repairs.caveat: Mining impacts, supply concentration, recycling, and grid integration remain serious constraints.

repairs.title: Social Protection Reached A Majority
repairs.summary: ILO estimates coverage by at least one social protection benefit rose from 42.8 percent in 2015 to 52.4 percent in 2023.
repairs.why_it_matters: More people have some protection against income loss caused by age, disability, unemployment, or family needs.
repairs.caveat: Nearly half the world remains uncovered, and the adequacy of benefits varies enormously.

repairs.title: Reading A Genome Became Affordable
repairs.summary: NHGRI data show the estimated cost of sequencing a human-sized genome fell by more than 100,000-fold between 2001 and 2022.
repairs.why_it_matters: A formerly enormous research task became usable at scale for biology, diagnosis, and disease surveillance.
repairs.caveat: The estimate covers sequence production, not interpretation, storage, privacy protection, or clinical care.

repairs.title: Flying Became Much Safer
repairs.summary: IATA's fatality-risk rate fell from 0.69 per million flight sectors in 2005 to 0.06 in 2024.
repairs.why_it_matters: Engineering standards, investigation, training, and shared reporting turned lessons from crashes into safer systems.
repairs.caveat: The rate rose from 2023 to 2024, and safety performance remains uneven between regions.

repairs.title: Humanity Moved An Asteroid
repairs.summary: NASA's DART impact shortened the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos's orbit by 32 minutes, proving a deflection technique works.
repairs.why_it_matters: Planetary defence moved from theory to a measured demonstration against a real object in space.
repairs.caveat: Dimorphos never threatened Earth, and one test cannot cover every asteroid type or warning scenario.

repairs.title: More Laws Opened Doors For Women
repairs.summary: The World Bank recorded 113 reforms in 68 economies strengthening women's economic opportunities from 2023 to 2025.
repairs.why_it_matters: Removing legal barriers can widen women's choices in work, pay, mobility, parenthood, assets, and business.
repairs.caveat: Laws are often incomplete or poorly enforced, and no assessed economy provides fully equal opportunity.
repairs.source_name: World Bank Women, Business and the Law

repairs.title: School Meals Reached More Children
repairs.summary: WFP reports 466 million children receive school meals worldwide, almost 80 million more than in 2020.
repairs.why_it_matters: A meal can improve attendance, learning, nutrition, and household security at the same time.
repairs.caveat: Coverage and meal quality remain uneven, especially in the poorest and conflict-affected countries.

repairs.title: Food Rules Cut A Hidden Heart Risk
repairs.summary: By 2023, 53 countries had best-practice industrial trans-fat policies covering 3.7 billion people.
repairs.why_it_matters: Changing food standards protects whole populations without requiring each person to identify a hidden ingredient.
repairs.caveat: More than half the world was still outside these protections, and enforcement determines their real effect.

repairs.title: Europe Grew While Emissions Fell
repairs.summary: From 1990 to 2023, EU net greenhouse-gas emissions fell 37% while its economy grew 70%.
repairs.why_it_matters: The long trend shows that economic growth and climate pollution do not have to rise together.
repairs.caveat: This is a domestic EU inventory that excludes international aviation and shipping; faster cuts are still needed.

repairs.title: Fewer Girls Faced Genital Cutting
repairs.summary: UNFPA reported that global prevalence of female genital mutilation fell by nearly a quarter from around 2000 to 2018.
repairs.why_it_matters: Community action, education, laws, and health work can weaken a deeply rooted practice that harms girls for life.
repairs.caveat: More than 230 million survivors are alive today, and progress remains far too slow to end the practice by 2030.

repairs.title: Nepal Nearly Tripled Its Tigers
repairs.summary: Nepal's wild tiger population rose from about 121 in 2009 to 355 in 2022, an increase of more than 190%.
repairs.why_it_matters: Protected habitat, anti-poaching work, and community involvement reversed a decline in one of the world's great predators.
repairs.caveat: More tigers also increase human-wildlife conflict, and the recovery depends on connected habitat and continued protection.

repairs.title: Cleaner Air Saved European Lives
repairs.summary: From 2005 to 2023, estimated premature deaths attributable to fine-particle pollution fell by 57% in the EU.
repairs.why_it_matters: Cleaner energy, transport, industry, and enforceable air rules translate into fewer early deaths.
repairs.caveat: The estimate still attributes about 182,000 premature deaths in 2023 to exposure above the WHO guideline.

repairs.title: Hurricane Paths Became Clearer
repairs.summary: The U.S. National Hurricane Center says its average storm-track forecast errors were cut in half over 15 years.
repairs.why_it_matters: Better forecasts give communities more precise warnings and more time to protect people and property.
repairs.caveat: Track forecasts do not remove uncertainty about intensity, rainfall, storm surge, or rapid strengthening.

repairs.title: Britain Ended Coal Power
repairs.summary: The United Kingdom's last coal-fired power station closed in September 2024 after coal use for electricity fell sharply from its 2012 peak.
repairs.why_it_matters: A country once built around coal removed it from electricity generation through policy, pricing, and replacement technologies.
repairs.caveat: This covers electricity, not all fossil-fuel use; gas remains important and the transition affected workers and communities.
repairs.source_name: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

repairs.title: Europe Treats Most Urban Wastewater
repairs.summary: By 2018, more than 90% of Europe's urban wastewater was collected and treated in line with EU standards.
repairs.why_it_matters: Sewers, treatment plants, funding, and common rules protect rivers, coasts, drinking water, and public health.
repairs.caveat: Compliance varies by country, millions still lack basic sanitation, and newer pollutants need more advanced treatment.

repairs.title: Mobile Broadband Reached Almost Everywhere
repairs.summary: In 2024, 96% of the world's population was covered by a 3G-or-better mobile network and 92% by 4G.
repairs.why_it_matters: Network coverage creates a path to communication, education, services, markets, and emergency information.
repairs.caveat: Coverage is not the same as affordable service or actual use; rural and low-income regions remain far behind.

repairs.title: More Girls Finished School
repairs.summary: From 2015 to 2022, girls' completion rose from 86% to 89% in primary school and from 54% to 61% in upper secondary school.
repairs.why_it_matters: Finishing school expands girls' choices, health, income, and ability to participate in decisions.
repairs.caveat: Millions of girls remain out of school, and completion does not guarantee equal learning, safety, or opportunity.
